result.rule: When the description names a human participant and an automated agent that acts on that participant's behalf, with each performing different activities and events within the same process: Model the human participant and the automated agent as separate lanes inside one participant pool, and place each activity and event in the lane of the party that performs it, including the start event and the task the human triggers. Do not leave the activities of either party unassigned to a lane.

When the description states that a person makes a choice on incoming items (for example accepting or denying them) and the generated model gives that human action its own task element that also needs a role or performer child: Keep every sequenceFlow as a direct child of the process (or subprocess) element, never inside the task that carries the human action. Put any resource or performer information for that task inside the task element itself, then list the sequence flows separately after all flow nodes in the owning process.

When the description states an action that an actor performs on an item or for another party in a sentence of its own, and that sentence does not state that the process must await a message, a signal, a time, or a condition: Model each such stated action as a task labelled with its verb and object, in the performing actor's lane, in the order the description gives. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event or an end event, and do not model it as a send task unless the description states a message exchange between separate participants.

When the description states that a party acts on the records or outputs of an earlier activity after they are stored or handed over, such as following up on them later: Model this follow-up as its own task, placed after the activity that produces the records and in the lane or pool of the party that performs it. Connect it in sequence from the producing or storing step so the follow-up is not dropped or merged into the earlier task.
